bevry.description: A web app for cocktail enthusiasts to discover, share, rate, and manage drinks.

project.title: The Project
text: Bevry is a web app created during my master's studies together with four fellow students. The application is aimed at cocktail enthusiasts who enjoy trying new drink creations and sharing their own recipes.
Initially, we focused on the basic functions: viewing, posting, liking, and rating cocktail recipes.

features.title: Features
text: In the second semester of the master's program, we gave the app a new design and added numerous new features to further improve the user experience.

With the new bar inventory feature, users can always keep track of their existing ingredients. Additionally, recommendations based on the ingredients available in the bar stock were integrated. The shopping list simplifies shopping by allowing missing ingredients to be added directly from the recipe. Users can now also create their own ingredients and add substitute ingredients to make recipes even more personalized.
For entertainment at parties, our two new mini-games come into play. One is the turn-based multiplayer game 'Spin the Wheel', and the other is the single-player game 'Mix it Up'.

branding.title: Branding
text: In the course 'Brand Identity & Corporate Design', the corporate identity of Bevry was developed. We worked with Adobe InDesign, Adobe Photoshop, and Figma.
I created the logo, various business stationery, stickers, website designs, and mockups.
Take a look at the brand book!

implementation.title: Implementation
text: The five of us worked with Scrum to organize ourselves. Sprint planning and sprint reviews took place every two weeks during our weekly meetings. We used Jira to create tickets and track their status on the Kanban board.

We also collaborated with fellow students from other master's programs, including 'Photography' for cocktail, marketing, and portfolio photos, 'Graphic Design' for app design and icons, 'Sound Design' for soundtracks and sound effects for the mini-games, and 'Animation' for a loading animation as well as animations within the mini-games.

myTasks.title: My Tasks
text: My main responsibility was in backend development with NestJS. Endpoint documentation was done using OpenAPI in Swagger. In the backend, I was responsible for the implementation of recipes, ingredients, substitute ingredients, as well as the shopping list and bar inventory. I also handled user data management and the implementation of email verification.
Additionally, I was involved in frontend development with Vue.js. I assisted in implementing the new screen designs and integrated both the self-designed icons and the loading animation.

erika.description: An app as a digital companion for climate-friendly actions and regional activities.

project.title: The Project
text: In the second semester of my master's program, I had the opportunity to work on a research project affiliated with the program's research institute. I chose the ERIKA project. The goal of the project is to develop the ERIKA app, which serves as a digital companion for climate-conscious actions in everyday life.

The app aims to promote climate-friendly behavior and highlight regional activities in the Waidhofen a/d Ybbs area. The focus is not only on sustainable content but also on sustainable aspects in the development and design of the app, ensuring a holistic implementation of the concept of sustainability.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: During my work on the ERIKA research project, I conducted extensive research on the factors crucial for developing a sustainable website.

Additionally, I participated in researching and formulating research questions related to climate-friendly actions in daily life, the impacts of various measures, the role of digitalization, and the application of gamification to support sustainable behavior.
I analyzed and processed survey results and created a clickable prototype of the app.

sustainability.title: Sustainable Web & App Design
text: In all areas of life, we strive for sustainability, but the environmental impact of the internet is often overlooked. The carbon emissions of the internet are equivalent to those of the aviation industry, accounting for about 2% of global emissions.

In my research on sustainable web, app, and email design, I discovered many aspects that contribute to sustainability. These include green hosting, SEO, design, UX, and performance optimization. For instance, choosing colors and fonts, writing efficient code, minimizing HTTP requests, optimizing images, and reducing third-party integrations can help lower the CO₂ footprint.

Sustainable web design is not only ecologically beneficial but also improves user experience, search engine ranking, and accessibility, particularly in regions with limited internet access. Websites that consume fewer resources load faster and offer better performance, enhancing user satisfaction and increasing reach.
I summarized the results of my research in a blog post.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
text: Additionally, I created a Figma prototype for a user story of the ERIKA service. This click dummy visualizes how the service can be used in everyday life to inform users about current sustainable initiatives.

The prototype includes a form through which users can submit their own initiatives. After review and approval, these initiatives appear in the calendar and map views. This allows users not only to participate in events but also to contribute their own ideas to increase their ecological handprint.

In the calendar and map views, users can see all upcoming initiatives and events, such as the weekly market or an upcoming flea market. Each event features a detailed view with a description and information about dates and locations. When GPS is enabled, users receive notifications when they are near an event.
